The vulnerability lies if the 'target_service' binary invokes this 'AuthorizedCommand' template, substituting '%s' with user-provided input, and passes the resulting string directly to a shell (e.g., via `sh -c`). By injecting shell metacharacters such as `";` (to end the current command) and `#` (to comment out the rest), we can execute arbitrary commands. Specifically, providing `"; cat /flag.txt #"` as input to 'target_service' will cause the effective command to become `/path/to/some_utility --arg ""; cat /flag.txt #"` which, when executed by a shell, will run `cat /flag.txt`.
